summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been very low and inconsistent, with long gaps between sessions and chronically short sleep (many nights under 5 hours) driving persistently low body battery scores — rarely above 60 and frequently in the 20–40 range. The most recent week (Sept 5–8) showed a positive uptick with meaningful bike and swim volume, suggesting a return to form, but the overall base heading into the Half Oceanman in 21 days is thin. With the 5,000m open-water swim just 3 weeks away as the immediate priority, the focus must be on consolidating swim fitness, managing fatigue carefully, and arriving rested rather than trying to cram volume.
suggestions: Sleep is the single biggest limiter right now — most nights are 4–6 hours and body battery is consistently depleted; prioritise 7–8 hours per night this week and next, as no training adaptation is worth the recovery deficit being accumulated.

With the Half Oceanman 5,000m swim 21 days away and your recent open-water sessions at ~28:30–28:47/100m pace, your target of 2:30/100m is achievable but will need 2–3 quality pool sessions before race day focusing on holding that pace continuously for 1,000m+ blocks.

The Sept 12 Wk12 long ride (110km, 240 min) is ambitious given your current fatigue state and proximity to the Half Oceanman — cap it at 60–75 km and 120 minutes at Z2 to avoid digging a recovery hole you can't climb out of before race day.

Running sessions in the pre-Oceanman taper window (Sept 19–Oct 3) should stay short and easy — the Half Oceanman is a swim-only event, so run legs need only be maintained, not built; keep efforts under 60 minutes at easy aerobic pace.

Post-Half Oceanman (Oct 4 onwards), your Treviso 10K is only 8 days later — plan at least 2–3 recovery days after the swim race before any quality run session, and treat the Oct 4 long run in the current plan as a definite skip if the Oceanman race leaves you fatigued.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk12 Long Ride: 110km @ 128–177W (Z2), 240 min, with optional 3x10min Z3 Tempo blocks
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 60–70km @ 120–145W (Z2 easy end), cap at 120 minutes — no tempo blocks; treat as aerobic maintenance only
proposed_changes.reason: With body battery consistently low, sleep chronically under 6 hours, and the Half Oceanman only 21 days away, a 4-hour ride risks a recovery hole that would compromise swim taper quality.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 10–12km @ 6:45–7:00/km easy, cap at 75 minutes — flat effort, no negative-split push
proposed_changes.reason: A 3-hour long run the day after a long ride, 20 days before the Half Oceanman swim, is excessive volume that will delay recovery without providing meaningful race-specific benefit.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk13 Evening session: 5x5min @ 210–244W (Z4 Threshold intervals), 90 min total
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with 45-minute Z2 endurance spin at 128–155W, flat and steady — no threshold work
proposed_changes.reason: Threshold cycling intervals 17 days before the Half Oceanman add intensity stress with no race-specific return; Z2 maintenance keeps legs fresh and aerobic fitness topped up.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk13 Pool Swim (Friday): 2,500–3,000m with 1,000m continuous block @ 2:30/100m and 4x200m @ 2:25/100m
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 2,000–2,500m total: 400m warm-up drills, 2x600m continuous @ 2:30/100m with 90s rest, 4x100m build, 200m cool-down — reduce interval intensity, keep pace honest
proposed_changes.reason: 13 days before the Half Oceanman this should be a confidence-building aerobic swim rather than a hard intensity session; the 2:25/100m 200m reps risk fatigue that undermines the taper.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk14 Evening session: 5x5min @ 210–244W (Z4 Threshold intervals), 90 min total
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip entirely or replace with 20-minute very easy spin at under 120W as a leg flush only — no structured intervals
proposed_changes.reason: Threshold intervals 8 days before the Half Oceanman are firmly inside the taper window and will leave residual fatigue that compromises race-day swim performance.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk15 Long Run: 21.5km @ 6:15–6:45/km, 180 min, the day after the Half Oceanman race
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip entirely — full rest or a 20-minute gentle walk only; assess fatigue before any decision on running at all
proposed_changes.reason: A 21.5km long run the morning after a 5,000m open-water race is a mandatory skip — the Treviso 10K is only 6 days later and residual swim fatigue plus a long run would eliminate any chance of racing it well.
